- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.03 to +0.37 in recent days).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows recent bearish momentum (e.g., -0.40 to -0.50).  
- Model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecasts by applying a 3-5 day moving average to sentiment-weighted price adjustments.  
- Avoid sharp upward revisions after a 3-5 day downtrend; price tends to mean-revert toward prior 10-day average.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.00 for 3+ days), reduce forecast volatility and shift toward lower end of historical range.  
- Overshoots in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–3) are common after spikes; cap forecast at 10% above prior 7-day high.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust quickly — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment lag.
